why: The book's printed working contradicts its own stem. The question asks how much CaO is produced; the derivation correctly divides 56 parts of CaO by 100 parts of CaCO3 and reaches 2.8 g — but the last line then labels that mass 'of CaCO3'. The VALUE is right and the SPECIES is wrong, and as printed the line asserts that decomposing 5 g of calcium carbonate produces 2.8 g of calcium carbonate. Corrected to CaO; an errata bracket names the defect. (The find/replace spans the whole final line rather than just the formula, so that both sides carry balanced \( \) delimiters.)

The book sets the part labels (a) and (b) inline in the middle of a sentence, so the printed line reads 'because it produces (a) smaller amount of (NH2)2CO) (b) The molar mass ...' — the (a) displaces the article 'a', there is an unmatched closing bracket, and part (b) begins mid-sentence with no break. As printed the sentence does not parse. Re-laid out so the (a)/(b)/(c) parts read as parts; no number, quantity or claim is changed.
find: because it produces (a) smaller amount of \((\mathrm{NH_2})_2\mathrm{CO}\)) (b) The molar mass
replace:
because it produces a smaller amount of \((\mathrm{NH_2})_2\mathrm{CO}\).

(b) The molar mass
